title: Macrovascular Permeability and Lipoprotein Flux Protocol
author: John Rutledge
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.yrrfv56

steps.title: Anesthetize Mice
steps.instruction: Anesthetize mice via intraperitoneal injection with 50 mg pentobarbital/kg weight.

steps.title: Collect and Process Blood
steps.instruction: Collect blood from the right atrium and prepare plasma samples.

substeps.instruction: Collect blood using a 22-gauge needle and a heparinized syringe.
Separate plasma samples from blood cells and store at 4°C.

steps.title: Flush Vasculature
steps.instruction: Flush the vasculature by infusing DMEM into the left ventricle of the heart.

steps.title: Dissect and Cannulate Artery
steps.instruction: Dissect and cannulate either the common carotid arteries or the aorta.

substeps.instruction: Make an anterior midline skin incision from the mandible to the sternum and retract superficial neck muscles to dissect carotid arteries free from surrounding tissue.
Make an incision in the proximal artery, insert a cannula (polyethylene-50 tubing), and tie it in place with 4-0 silk.
Make a second incision in the distal portion of the artery, just proximal to the bifurcation of the common carotid artery, and insert and tie a second cannula.

steps.title: Perfuse and Maintain Artery
steps.instruction: Perfuse the artery with Kreb’s-Henseleit solution plus 1% bovine serum albumin (BSA) gassed with 95% compressed air and 5% CO2 until the start of the experiment.

substeps.instruction: Maintain the artery at a constant length from the moment of cannulation until it is secured in the perfusion chamber.

steps.title: Mount Artery for Imaging
steps.instruction: Place the cannulated artery in a clear fluid-filled superfusate chamber and mount it on a Nikon MM-11 upright microscope stage.

steps.title: Configure Perfusion Parameters
steps.instruction: Set the perfusion system to a physiological flow rate (1.5-2ml/min) and hydrostatic pressure (90 cm H2O), maintaining all perfusates at 37°C and pH 7.3-7.4.

substeps.instruction: Prepare perfusate options: a. Clear, non-fluorescent Kreb’s-Henseleit solution with 1% BSA; b. FITC- or TRITC-labeled Dextran or Albumin at 40-70 µg/mL in Kreb’s-Henseleit solution with 1% BSA; c. DiL or Alex-546 labeled lipid particles at 50 µg/mL in Kreb’s-Henseleit solution with 1% BSA.

steps.title: Set Up Fluorescence Detection
steps.instruction: Bring the artery in the superfusate chamber into focus using a Nikon Plan X4 objective (NA 0.1).

substeps.instruction: Excite the fluorophore and measure emission using a Nikon P1 photometer.
Input data to a chart recorder and computer, and visualize via Hamamatsu CCD television and camera.

steps.title: Establish Baseline Fluorescence
steps.instruction: Perfuse the artery with the nonfluorescent solution to determine the baseline level of fluorescence intensity (If).

steps.title: Perform Fluorescent Perfusion and Washout
steps.instruction: Perfuse the artery with the buffer solution containing the fluorescently labeled compound (FLC) for 10 min, followed immediately by a 10 min washout with the clear non-fluorescent solution.

substeps.instruction: For Permeability: Use FITC- or TRITC-labeled albumin or dextran.
For Lipoprotein Flux: Use DiL or Alex546 labeled lipoproteins.

steps.title: Calculate Flux
steps.instruction: Calculate the flux (ng/min/cm²) using the measured fluorescence intensities.

substeps.instruction: Define If0 as initial fluorescence intensity of the solution filling the artery lumen and IfA as the change in fluorescent intensity between baseline (If) and after washout (accumulation), both in milliVolts (mV).
Calculate Artery Volume (V = πr²l) and Artery Surface Area (SA = 2πrl).
Determine ng in vessel at If0: Artery V * [FLC in ng/mL].
Determine ng/mV: (ng in vessel at If0) / If0 (mV).
Determine ng compound at IfA: (ng/mV) * IfA (mV).
Calculate final flux: (ng of compound at IfA) / time(min) / Artery SA = ng/min/cm².
